messages.subject: legend labels order
parts:
Hi,

 

I have made a plot with the code shown here below, which renders the attached figure. My question is: is there a way in which the colours and labels on the legend would follow the order of the colours on the plot, i.e. "darkred", "red", "green" and "darkgreen".? I have not been able to get to it and it is driving me nuts! Thanks a lot!!

 

David Rengel


ggplot(mydata, aes(dpi), ylim(min(mydata$Freq2):max(mydata$Freq2))) + 

  geom_bar(data = subset(mydata, Above_Below == "Above"), 

           aes(y = Freq2, fill = Diff2, color=Diff2), stat = "identity", position = "stack") +

  geom_bar(data = subset(mydata, Above_Below == "Below"), 

           aes(y = Freq2, fill = Diff2, color=Diff2), stat = "identity", position = "stack") +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NegFC>2" = "darkgreen", "NegFC<2" = "green", "PosFC>2" = "darkred", "PosFC<2" = "red")) +

  scale_color_manual(values =  c("NegFC>2" = "darkgreen", "NegFC<2" = "green", "PosFC>2" = "darkred", "PosFC<2" = "red")) +

  labs(y = "# of DEGs") +

  facet_grid(~comp)

parts:
> I have made a plot with the code shown here below, which renders the
> attached figure. My question is: is there a way in which the colours and
> labels on the legend would follow the order of the colours on the plot,
> i.e. "darkred", "red", "green" and "darkgreen".? I have not been able to
> get to it and it is driving me nuts! Thanks a lot!!

If you make Freq2 a factor with the levels ordered as you want, that
should do it. See ?factor , ?reorder or maybe something from the forcats
package if you're working in the tidyverse.

Ron.

messages.author: 0789541932753d34
messages.subject: Re: legend labels order
parts:
Hi Ron,
Tanks a lot. I guess you meant Diff2, and not Freq2. Here below there is a code telling how I created  Diff2 and, now, Diff3 with te reordered labels. It does not change the colour order on the legend but, worse, it messes up the colour on the plot. (see the attached figure). I wonder what am I missing here.Thanks again.

mydata$Diff2 <- as.character(mydata$Diff)
mydata$Diff2 <- sub("-1","NegFC<2",mydata$Diff2)
mydata$Diff2[which(mydata$Diff==-2)] <- "NegFC>2"
mydata$Diff2[which(mydata$Diff==1)] <- "PosFC<2"
mydata$Diff2[which(mydata$Diff==2)] <- "PosFC>2"
mydata$Diff3 <- factor(mydata$Diff2,levels = c("NegFC>2","NegFC<2","PosFC<2","PosFC>2"))
mydata$Diff2 <- factor(mydata$Diff2,levels = c("PosFC>2","PosFC<2","NegFC>2","NegFC<2"))
